archMap.why: no i386 programs: libseccomp turns the socket rules into socketcall rules without the family test, which would reopen AF_ALG (CVE-2026-31431)

remove.name: socketcall
remove.why: the socket(2) multiplexer hides the socket family behind a pointer seccomp cannot read, so it would bypass the AF_ALG refusal (CVE-2026-31431)

remove.name: vmsplice
remove.why: maps user pages into a pipe by reference, the path of a run of kernel exploits (CVE-2008-0600 and Dirty Pipe's family); lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

remove.name: cachestat
remove.why: tells which pages of any file it can open are in the host's page cache, a side channel on what other containers read; lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

remove.name: map_shadow_stack
remove.why: x86 user shadow stacks are off in lea and glibc runs without them; lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

remove.name: futex_waitv
remove.why: futex2 (Linux 5.16), which glibc does not call (only Wine and Proton do); lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

remove.name: futex_wake
remove.why: futex2 (Linux 6.7), which glibc does not call; lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

remove.name: futex_wait
remove.why: futex2 (Linux 6.7), which glibc does not call; lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

remove.name: futex_requeue
remove.why: futex2 (Linux 6.7), which glibc does not call; futex requeue is where CVE-2014-3153 was; lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

remove.name: io_pgetevents
remove.why: the legacy Linux AIO interface, which no tool lea ships uses; lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

remove.name: io_pgetevents_time64
remove.why: the 32-bit-time io_pgetevents (no x86_64 or aarch64 number); lea's profile before #100 refused it (EPERM), with no workload of lea needing it since

allow.name: clone
allow.why: the nested Podman and crun create the user, mount, PID, network and IPC namespaces of nested containers, flags moby allows only with CAP_SYS_ADMIN

allow.name: unshare
allow.why: rootless Podman enters its user namespace (CLONE_NEWUSER), unpacks image layers in a mount namespace, and Buildah's RUN steps unshare their own

allow.name: setns
allow.why: every podman command joins the user namespace of Podman's pause process, and podman exec and pasta join a nested container's namespaces

allow.name: mount
allow.why: crun mounts a nested container's root file system, /proc, /dev and volumes, fuse-overlayfs its layers and pasta its empty tmpfs root, inside the nested user namespace

allow.name: umount2
allow.why: crun and pasta detach the old root after pivot_root, and Podman unmounts a nested container's storage, shm and network namespace

allow.name: open_tree
allow.why: crun clones the /sys of lea into a nested container (OPEN_TREE_CLONE): a user namespace cannot mount a fresh sysfs without its own network namespace's ownership of it

allow.name: move_mount
allow.why: crun attaches the trees it cloned with open_tree (/sys, bind mounts) inside a nested container

allow.name: mount_setattr
allow.why: crun sets the flags of the trees it cloned (read-only /sys, read-only and nosuid bind mounts), recursively

allow.name: pivot_root
allow.why: crun switches a nested container to its own root file system, and pasta sandboxes itself in an empty tmpfs

narrow.why: AF_NETLINK (16) sockets stay allowed but for NETLINK_AUDIT (9), which lea's NETLINK_AUDIT rule refuses: an allow rule overlapping it would make crun refuse the profile (EEXIST)

rules.why: AF_ALG (38), the kernel crypto API, gets EAFNOSUPPORT, the answer of a kernel without it (CVE-2026-31431); moby leaves it out of its socket families

NETLINK_AUDIT (AF_NETLINK 16, protocol 9) gets EINVAL, as in lea's profile before #100 and in Docker's without CAP_AUDIT_WRITE, which lea drops: the host's audit subsystem is not namespaced and nothing in lea talks to it
